title: Iteratively weighted least squares
dek: IRLS / IWLS fits a GLM by repeating weighted OLS on a working response. Gaussian identity OLS is the algorithm that finishes in one step.
story: A GLM log-likelihood is generally not a quadratic in β. Fisher scoring linearises the score and solves a weighted least-squares problem at each step. The working response is z = η + (y − μ) g′(μ), with weights W = 1 / (V(μ) [g′(μ)]²).

Each iteration: compute μ(β_old), build z and W, regress z on X with weights W, get β_new. Stop when the score is numerically zero. That is IRLS. Newton uses the observed Hessian instead of expected information; for canonical links they often coincide.

This is why GLM software feels like regression: it is regression, iterated, in a metric the family chose. It is also why starting values, complete separation, and exploding weights are numerical siblings of scientific problems (perfect prediction, μ̂ on the boundary).
deep: At convergence, Var̂(β̂) ≈ (Xᵀ W X)⁻¹ φ, with W evaluated at μ̂. Those weights are Fisher information in disguise. Quasi-likelihood keeps the same IRLS and replaces φ or V(μ) without a full pmf.

Canonical Bernoulli: g′(μ) = 1/(μ(1−μ)), V(μ) = μ(1−μ), so W = μ(1−μ). Points with μ̂ near 0 or 1 get tiny weight — the algorithm itself downweights sure events. That is information, not a bug, until complete separation makes μ̂ hit 0/1 and W collapse.
Offsets enter η before z is built. Observation weights (survey weights) multiply W. Do not confuse survey weights with IRLS working weights; they can both be present.
Failure to converge is a result. Report it. Firth / penalised logistic, exact logistic, or a Bayesian prior with positive curvature are the usual scientific exits, not “more iterations.”

example.title: One IRLS step for a Bernoulli intercept-only model

steps.title: Weighted OLS
steps.body: Equal weights, intercept-only: β_new = z̄ = 0. Already the MLE (logit of 0.5). The algorithm noticed immediately because the start was the truth for this balanced sample.

steps.title: If y were (0,0,0,1)
steps.body: Start at 0.5, one step moves toward logit(0.25). Later steps refine. If y were (0,0,0,0), weights collapse toward 0 and you meet the boundary problem.

example.takeaway: IRLS is weighted projection of a working z. When W dies, the likelihood is telling you about the edge of Θ.

check.prompt: Gaussian identity GLM makes IRLS collapse to one OLS fit because:
choices: W is constant and z = y, so the working regression is OLS on the original outcome
check.answer: W is constant and z = y, so the working regression is OLS on the original outcome
check.why: g′ = 1, V = 1 (or σ² absorbed in φ). No iteration needed.

whyWrong.Projections are illegal in GLMs: IRLS is a sequence of projections.

check.prompt: Canonical logit, μ = 0.2. Working weight W = μ(1−μ) equals:

whyWrong.0.2: The mean, not the Bernoulli variance.

check.prompt: On the IRLS flow plate, the back-arrow “not yet” means:
check.figureHint: Loop from weighted OLS back to μ, η.
choices: The algorithm is drawing a posterior
β_new is used to rebuild μ, z, W until the score is numerically zero
You must randomise rows each iteration
check.answer: β_new is used to rebuild μ, z, W until the score is numerically zero
check.why: That is iteration. Convergence is a score ≈ 0 statement.

whyWrong.The algorithm is drawing a posterior: IRLS is frequentist scoring (or a MAP if you added a penalty).
